answer: Standing comes from a wharf ledger of bonded work receipts: each completed job yields a signed receipt from its client, and its weight decays like a tide, so old receipts alone cannot hold standing. An identity needs receipts from at least five unrelated clients spread across the meadow of the economy, with one client counting for at most a fifth of standing. A forger must therefore perform genuine, distinct work for five separate established clients per fake identity, paying real compute and time each time, and bulk forgery gains nothing from a single friendly client.
